CHICAGO, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Equity LifeStyle Properties, Inc. (

) (referred to herein as "we," "us," and "our") today announced results for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All per share results are reported on a fully diluted basis unless otherwise noted.

Normalized FFO per Common Share and OP Unit for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $0.79, representing a 4.6% increase compared to the same period in 2025, consistent with the midpoint of our previous guidance range of $0.76 to $0.82. Core property operating revenues increased 4.4%, Core property operating expenses, excluding property management, increased 1.3% and Core income from property operations, excluding property management, increased 6.7% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, each as compared to the same period in 2025. Normalized FFO for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $2.36 per Common Share and OP Unit, representing a 4.0% increase compared to the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Core property operating revenues increased 4.3%, Core property operating expenses, excluding property management, increased 2.0% and Core income from property operations, excluding property management, increased 6.0%, each as compared to the same period in 2025.

Core MH base rental income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 5.7% compared to the same period in 2025, which is 0.1% higher than the midpoint of our previous guidance range. Occupied sites increased by 99 and new and used home sales totaled 244 during the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Core MH base rental income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 5.7% compared to the same period in 2025. Occupied sites increased by 166 and new and used home sales totaled 707 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Core RV and marina base rental income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 2.1% compared to the same period in 2025, which is 0.4% higher than the midpoint of our previous guidance range. Core RV and marina annual base rental income increased 5.3% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Core annual membership subscriptions for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 8.4% compared to the same period in 2025.

Core RV and marina base rental income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 0.8% compared to the same period in 2025. Core RV and marina annual base rental income increased 5.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Core annual membership subscriptions for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 10.2% as compared to the same period in 2025.

In aggregate, Core RV and marina annual base rental income and annual membership subscriptions for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased by 5.8% and 5.9%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.

Core property operating expenses, excluding property management, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 1.3% compared to the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Core property operating expenses, excluding property management, increased 2.0% compared to the same period in 2025.
Our preliminary 2027 Core MH base rent income growth assumption is approximately 5.1%.
Our preliminary 2027 Core RV annual rent income growth assumption is approximately 4.7%.

The preliminary 2027 rent growth assumptions reflect management's best estimate of the most likely outcome based on our current view of existing market conditions and assumptions. See Forward-Looking Statements in this news release for factors impacting our preliminary 2027 rent growth assumptions. By October month-end, we anticipate sending 2027 rent increase notices to approximately 50% of our MH residents. We have set RV annual rates for more than 95% of our annual sites. These increases will take effect at the start of the 2026/27 winter season or the start of the 2027 summer season, as applicable. Our rent growth assumptions do not include contribution from incremental sites that may be occupied in 2027.

Fourth quarter and full year 2026 guidance presented below represent management's estimate of a range of possible outcomes. The midpoint of the ranges reflect management's estimate of the most likely outcome based on our current view of existing market conditions and assumptions. Full year 2026 guidance ranges, including Core portfolio growth rate ranges, have been narrowed to reflect actual results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, leaving only fourth quarter results subject to estimate. Actual results could vary materially from management's estimate if any of our assumptions are incorrect. See Forward-Looking Statements in this news release for factors impacting our 2026 guidance assumptions. See Non-GAAP Financial Measures Definitions and Reconciliations at the end of the Supplemental Financial Information for additional information.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures Definitions and Reconciliations

The following Non-GAAP financial measures definitions do not include adjustments in respect to membership upgrade revenue: (i) FFO; (ii) Normalized FFO; (iii) EBITDAre; (iv) Adjusted EBITDAre; (v) Property operating revenues; (vi) Property operating expenses, excluding property management; and (vii) Income from property operations, excluding property management.

We define FFO as net income, computed in accordance with GAAP, excluding gains or losses from sales of properties, depreciation and amortization related to real estate, impairment charges and adjustments to reflect our share of FFO of unconsolidated joint ventures. Adjustments for unconsolidated joint ventures are calculated to reflect FFO on the same basis. We compute FFO in accordance with our interpretation of standards established by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts ("NAREIT"), which may not be comparable to FFO reported by other REITs that do not define the term in accordance with the current NAREIT definition or that interpret the current NAREIT definition differently than we do.

We believe FFO, as defined by the Board of Governors of NAREIT, is generally a measure of performance for an equity REIT. While FFO is a relevant and widely used measure of operating performance for equity REITs, it does not represent cash flow from operations or net income as defined by GAAP, and it should not be considered as an alternative to these indicators in evaluating liquidity or operating performance.

We define Normalized FFO as FFO excluding non-operating income and expense items, such as gains and losses from early debt extinguishment, including prepayment penalties, defeasance costs, transaction/pursuit costs and other, expenses and benefits related to deferred tax valuation allowances and reversals, and other miscellaneous non-comparable items. Normalized FFO presented herein is not necessarily comparable to Normalized FFO presented by other real estate companies due to the fact that not all real estate companies use the same methodology for computing this amount.
We define FAD as Normalized FFO less non-revenue producing capital expenditures.

We believe that FFO, Normalized FFO and FAD are helpful to investors as supplemental measures of the performance of an equity REIT. We believe that by excluding the effect of gains or losses from sales of properties, depreciation and amortization related to real estate and impairment charges, which are based on historical costs and may be of limited relevance in evaluating current performance, FFO can facilitate comparisons of operating performance between periods and among other equity REITs. We further believe that Normalized FFO provides useful information to investors, analysts and our management because it allows them to compare our operating performance to the operating performance of other real estate companies and between periods on a consistent basis without having to account for differences not related to our normal operations. For example, we believe that excluding the early extinguishment of debt and other miscellaneous non-comparable items from FFO allows investors, analysts and our management to assess the sustainability of operating performance in future periods because these costs do not affect the future operations of the properties. In some cases, we provide information about identified non-cash components of FFO and Normalized FFO because it allows investors, analysts and our management to assess the impact of those items.
INCOME FROM PROPERTY OPERATIONS, EXCLUDING PROPERTY MANAGEMENT.

We define Income from property operations, excluding property management as rental income, membership subscriptions and upgrade sales, utility and other income less property and rental home operating and maintenance expenses, real estate taxes, membership sales and marketing expenses, excluding property management expenses. Property management represents the expenses associated with indirect costs such as off-site payroll and certain administrative and professional expenses. We believe exclusion of property management expenses is helpful to investors and analysts as a measure of the operating results of our properties, excluding items that are not directly related to the operation of the properties. For comparative purposes, we present bad debt expense within insurance and other in the current and prior periods. We believe that this Non-GAAP financial measure is helpful to investors and analysts as a measure of the operating results of our properties.

EARNINGS BEFORE INTEREST, TAX, DEPRECIATION AND AMORTIZATION FOR REAL ESTATE (EBITDAre) AND ADJUSTED EBITDAre.

We define EBITDAre as net income or loss excluding interest income and expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, gains or losses from sales of properties, impairment charges, and adjustments to reflect our share of EBITDAre of unconsolidated joint ventures. We compute EBITDAre in accordance with our interpretation of the standards established by NAREIT, which may not be comparable to EBITDAre reported by other REITs that do not define the term in accordance with the current NAREIT definition or that interpret the current NAREIT definition differently than we do.

We define Adjusted EBITDAre as EBITDAre excluding non-operating income and expense items, such as gains and losses from early debt extinguishment, including prepayment penalties and defeasance costs, transaction/pursuit costs and other, and other miscellaneous non-comparable items.

We believe that EBITDAre and Adjusted EBITDAre may be useful to an investor in evaluating our operating performance and liquidity because the measures are widely used to measure the operating performance of an equity REIT.
